newsitem.title: USA: Families of downed fliers sue Cuban government.
newsitem.headline: Families of downed fliers sue Cuban government.

text.p: The families of three Cuban exiles killed when Cuban jets shot down their planes over the Florida Straits filed suits against Cuba's government and airforce on Thursday.

"We exercise this right as American citizens in order to seek justice for the brutal killings of our family members and in hopes of deterring similar acts of brutality against other U.S. citizens," Marlene Alejandre, the widow of Armando Alejandre, told a news conference.
Aaron Podhurst, lawyer for the families, insisted the civil action suit was not a symbolic gesture even though it was unlikely any Cuban official would show up in a U.S. court.

Cuban MiG jets shot down two small planes belonging to Brothers to the Rescue, a Miami-based Cuban exile group that searches for people fleeing the communist-ruled island by sea on Feb. 24. All four men in the planes were killed.
Cuba said the planes were over its airspace but the International Civil Aviation Organsiation (ICAO) backed the U.S. position that they were over international waters.
The action drew international condemnation and infuriated Miami's exile communty, which over the years has mounted a sustained campaign against Cuban President Fidel Castro.
Brothers to the Rescue said the planes were on a humanitarian mission. In the past its planes have dropped political leaflets over Havana.
Alejandre, with the black-clad families of Carlos Costa and Mario de la Pena alongsside her, said: "The void caused by Armando, Carlos and Mario's deaths is impossible to fill...
"We owe it to them to do everything in our power to hold those responsible for their deaths fully accountable."

The suits, filed in a U.S. district court in Miami, were brought under a 1996 anti-terrorist law which allows U.S. citizens to take action for killings outside the United States as result of "state-sponsored terrorism".
The family of the fourth victim, Pablo Morales, were unable to file a suit as he was not a U.S. citizen.
Any damages could be paid out of Cuban assets frozen in the United States.
